newsitem.title: UK: Russian debt nosedives on Yeltsin health news.
newsitem.headline: Russian debt nosedives on Yeltsin health news.

text.p: Russian debt took a nosedive on news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin was not well enough to have his planned heart operation this month, reversing the market euphoria of early last week, traders said.
"People have known he was weak but this morning they just started panicking," said one trader at a US firm in London.
"The doctors saying he has a 50-50 chance of survival is the scary thing, and people are worried about the debt rescheduling deal going through, and about the Eurobond," the trader added.
Russian mark Vnesh loans RUVNDMLNS=RR shed 1-1/2 in early trading, falling to 68-7/8 on the news, while the Min Fin 4 fell 1-1/4 to 50-00.
But another trader said there had been some buying of the Min Fins at these lower levels from domestic Russian investors.
Traders said the spread between the dollar and mark Vnesh loans had gone askew, narrowing to 3-1/2, amid the anxieties.
Dealers are waiting for a credit rating for Russia, to be awarded ahead of its planned Eurobond launch. But some players are worried about whether the dollar-denominated bond will go ahead on time.
This morning's Russian debt levels mark a reversal from the first half of last week, when dollar Vnesh loans hit an all-time high at 71-1/2.
Bulgarian debt also continued in its depressed mode, with FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR shedding 1/4 point to 30-1/8 in a market alive with rumours.
But when Bulgaria jacked up its main interest rate to 300 percent from 108 percent prices began to inch back.
Philippine debt was largely unchanged after the announcement of the level of its Brady exchange rate, at 2.25 percent over US Treasuries for the 20-year issue.
The Philippines is exchanging its 2017 and 2018 fixed rate bonds for new dollar-denominated fixed rate bonds due in 2016.

With most traders focusing heavily on eastern Europe, Latin America was mostly flat to 1/8 softer. Argentine Pars AR4C23=RR were a touch weaker at 56-1/2 in the run up to Thursday's general strike, and Brazil C's BR8D14=RR were also off a fraction at 68-3/8.
Mexican paper also slipped 1/8, with Pars MX625L19=RR at 68-1/2.

Most players were standing on the sidelines ahead of tomorrow's FOMC meeting which could see US rates lifted 25 basis points. Mexico and Argentina are likely to be affected most by any rate move. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
